name: forma
description: Turn a screenshot, a PDF, or an existing report into a real DevExpress .repx — AI-generated spec, in-browser mockup, and XtraReports XML. Bring your own Gemini key.
comment:overrides: qs: two Dependabot advisories (array-limit bypass, DoS via attacker-controlled isBuffer) are fixed in 6.16.0, and four consumers declare ranges that still admit an affected version. The one that settles it is this project's own express@4: 4.22.2 asks for ~6.15.1, which can only resolve to an affected version. express@5 (^6.14.0, via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk), exegesis (^6.6.0) and googleapis-common (^6.7.0, both via firebase-tools) merely allow one. `npm audit fix` cannot lift them without a breaking change, so the override pins every copy instead. Every qs in the tree was already 6.x, so this is a patch-level lift, not a major. body-parser 2.4.0 asks for ^6.16.1, a floor above this override's, but 6.16.1 is what resolves, so nothing is lowered in practice. Remove this entry once no consumer's own range admits a version below 6.16.0. `npm explain qs` is the check: it prints each consumer as overridden ... (was <its own range>). `npm ls qs --all` cannot answer it, because it shows versions after the override has been applied. sharp (2026-11-06): three high Dependabot advisories, in the librsvg, libheif and libvips it bundles, are fixed in 0.35.5, and its only consumer, @huggingface/transformers, asks for ^0.34.1 in every 3.x release (3.7.6 is installed). transformers 4.3.2 asks for ^0.35.4, but that is a major upgrade of the handwriting reader and moves onnxruntime-web to a dev build, so the override lifts sharp alone. A 0.34 to 0.35 move is semver-major for a 0.x package, and it is safe here for a reason qs did not need: nothing ever loads sharp. Forma imports Transformers.js only in the browser (src/lib/handwriting.ts), where the package resolves to dist/transformers.web.js, which does not import sharp, and nothing that runs under Node imports Transformers.js at all. Its install script is denied in allowScripts below, so the override changes only which files sit in node_modules. It was checked anyway: under Node, Transformers.js 3.7.6 still reads an image through sharp 0.35.5 (RawImage.read, with the install script denied). Remove this entry when @huggingface/transformers moves to a release whose own range reaches 0.35.5; `npm explain sharp` is the check, as for qs.
comment:not-overridden: @grpc/grpc-js, uuid, @opentelemetry/core and minimatch carry Dependabot advisories and are deliberately NOT overridden. @grpc/grpc-js (two highs, fixed in 1.13.6) is pinned ~1.9.0 by @firebase/firestore, in 4.14.0 and still in 4.17.2, so no firebase release in range fixes it, and an override would push another package's internals four minors past the range it asked for. It is Firestore's Node.js transport -- the browser entry never imports it -- so here it runs only in the rules tests, against the local emulator. It is also the whole reason firebase, both Firestore packages and @firebase/rules-unit-testing are flagged high. uuid (9.0.1 via gaxios -> 11.1.1) and @opentelemetry/core (1.30.1 via @google-cloud/pubsub -> 2.8.0) live inside firebase-tools, already the latest published version (15.34.1 as of 2026-10-24, 15.34.2 on 2026-11-04 and still carrying both; 15.35.0, the latest on 2026-11-06 and not yet installed, asks for the same gaxios, google-auth-library and @google-cloud/pubsub ranges), so the fix has to come from upstream. minimatch (one medium, Dependabot #53, opened 2026-11-06: denial of service through globparts amplification in >=7.0.0 <11.0.1, fixed in 11.0.1) is the same case. The affected copy is 9.0.9, which glob 10 asks for as ^9.0.4, and glob 10 comes in through firebase-tools itself and, inside it, through archiver (via archiver-utils), exegesis and rimraf (via google-gax and @google-cloud/pubsub); 15.35.0 still asks for glob ^10.5.0. The other three copies, 3.1.5, 5.1.9 and 6.2.3, are below the affected range. 11.0.1 is two majors past what glob asks for, so that fix has to come from upstream as well. firebase itself stays at 12.12.1 on purpose: `npm audit fix` moved it to 12.19.0 within its range on 2026-11-04, which fixed no advisory (its Firestore still pins @grpc/grpc-js ~1.9.0) and grew the Firestore chunk every signed-in visitor downloads from under 478,000 bytes to 668,704, so it was put back. Only firebase-tools' own in-range fixes were kept. That is how csv-parse and stream-json closed: they were listed here until 15.34.1 bumped them itself. Forcing a major into firebase-tools is a different proposition from the patch-level qs lift above, because it runs the Firestore emulator that `npm run test:rules` depends on, and breaking it takes 70 security-rule tests with it. Leave the alerts OPEN rather than dismissing them: an open alert closes itself when upstream bumps its dependencies, a dismissed one stays silent forever. minimatch's #53 is left open on that reasoning. The older three are not open any more: the owner's account dismissed @grpc/grpc-js's #45 and #46 and uuid's #1 as not used on 2026-10-28, each with its reason written on the alert, and Dependabot auto-dismissed @opentelemetry/core's #2, a development dependency, on 2026-09-09. None of them will close or reappear on its own when upstream fixes it, so npm audit, which still lists all three, and the command below are where they show. Re-check with `npm ls @grpc/grpc-js uuid @opentelemetry/core minimatch --all` before acting on this.
comment:allowScripts: npm 11.19 warns on every install about dependencies whose install scripts nobody has reviewed. These five were reviewed and approved on 2026-10-24, and all of them had already been running on every install. re2 is the only one doing real work: node-gyp compiles its native binding, an optional dependency of superstatic inside firebase-tools. esbuild (0.28.2 directly, 0.25.12 via vite) verifies its platform binary. protobufjs only prints a version-scheme warning, and @firebase/util only acts when FIREBASE_WEBAPP_CONFIG is set, which App Hosting uses and this project does not. Entries are pinned to versions, npm's default, so a script whose code changes gets reviewed again. After an update, `npm install-scripts ls` names what needs approving and `npm install-scripts prune` drops entries no longer installed. Its --dry-run flag wrote this block anyway on npm 11.19.0, so do not rely on it to preview. tesseract.js (OCR, 2026-11-01) is reviewed and DENIED, for every version: its postinstall is opencollective-postinstall, which only prints a funding message, and nothing it does is needed; the engine's files are copied at build by vite.config.ts instead. onnxruntime-node and sharp (handwriting, 2026-11-04) are reviewed and DENIED, for every version: both arrive with @huggingface/transformers for Node, onnxruntime-node's postinstall fetches native and GPU binaries and sharp's checks or builds its image library, and Forma runs Transformers.js only in the browser, on onnxruntime-web, where neither is used. Since 2026-11-10 onnxruntime-node is also a devDependency, imported by the measuring scripts (scripts/model/paddleOcr.ts) on the CPU binaries its package ships for every platform: the denied postinstall only downloads the Linux CUDA ones, so nothing they need is lost.
